content_html:
Embedded Memory — Select · Change · Reconstruct

Integrates the idea of embedded memory with the core framework — Select → Change → Reconstruct — across neural, embodied, contextual, and social levels.

Embeddedness is a continuous substrate underneath Select (encoding in context and emotion), Change (plasticity and reconsolidation), and Reconstruct (cue/state-dependent retrieval and narrative integration).

  • Select: Encoding is context dependent (encoding specificity). Emotional arousal (amygdala) tags traces for priority consolidation.
  • Change: Each act of recall triggers reconsolidation, updating the trace and its associations; systems consolidation transforms hippocampal traces into distributed neocortex over time.
  • Reconstruct: Retrieval is cue- and state-dependent; reconstruction integrates distributed fragments, or remains fragmented (e.g., trauma) until re-embedded into coherent narrative.
Scale Mechanism Illustration
Neural Synaptic plasticity; hippocampal–cortical systems; amygdala modulation Emotion-tagged episodic encoding; transformation over months/years
Embodied Procedural learning in basal ganglia, cerebellum, motor cortex “Body remembers” bike-riding
Contextual Encoding specificity; context/state-dependent cues Divers recall best where they learned (land vs. underwater)
Social Collective narratives scaffold recall Rituals, family stories as external memory cues
